mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine typically costs £1,200-£4,500 supply-only, depending on whether you have the 4B11 (2.0L), 4B12 (2.4L), or 4N14 diesel. Fitted prices add £500-£1,100 for labour. Used engines: £600-£1,800. Reconditioned: £1,200-£3,800. Rebuilt with warranty: £1,800-£5,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV 4B11?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first and most common warning sign is a metallic rattle or clatter from the engine on cold start, lasting a few seconds before oil pressure builds. If ignored, you may hear a constant rattle, experience loss of power, and eventually the engine warning light will illuminate. Catastrophic failure results in the engine cutting out completely and potential valve/piston damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the vehicle's value and condition justify the investment. A Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV with good battery health, low to medium mileage, and no other major issues is well worth replacing. For 2013-2018 models valued over £6,000, a rebuilt 4B11 engine (£1,800-£3,500 supply-only) is a sound investment. For 2018+ models with the 4B12 engine and values over £10,000, replacement is almost always financially sensible.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine replacement typically takes 8-12 hours for a specialist, so allow 1-2 working days for the job. Your vehicle will be off the road for this period. Most specialists can complete the job within 2 working days. Some offer a collection and delivery service for convenience. Supply-only engines are dispatched within 1-3 working days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV 2.0L and 2.4L engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The key difference is displacement and power: the 4B11 (2013-2018) produces 118hp from 2.0L, while the 4B12 (2018-present) produces 135hp from 2.4L. The 4B12 is generally more robust and less prone to timing chain issues, but can suffer oil consumption from piston ring wear on higher-mileage units.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a rebuilt Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt and reconditioned engine supplied through EnginesMarket's UK network carries a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Terms vary by specialist - some offer 24-month or 36-month warranties on premium rebuilds. 12-month unlimited mileage is the minimum standard. Extended warranties available on some specialist rebuilds. Always confirm exact warranty terms before ordering.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched in 2013 as the world's first plug-in hybrid SUV, the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV paired a 2.0-litre petrol engine with two electric motors for a unique hybrid driving experience. The powertrain evolved through two main generations, with the 2.4-litre 4B12 replacing the 2.0-litre 4B11 from 2018.

milestones.description: 4B11, 2.0L MIVEC petrol, 118hp, paired with two 60kW electric motors for 200hp combined output
4B12, 2.4L MIVEC petrol, 135hp, paired with twin electric motors for 224hp combined output, introduced with facelift
PHEV system updated with larger 13.8kWh battery, improved EV range, same 4B12 engine
New generation Outlander PHEV launched with different platform and powertrain architecture

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV's 4B11 and 4B12 petrol engines are generally reliable but have known weak points. The 4B11 timing chain tensioner and the 4B12 oil consumption issues are the most common reasons owners seek replacement engines through our network. Rebuilt engines from EnginesMarket specialists include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV 4B11 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The 4B11's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, leading to chain slack and eventual failure if not addressed. Cold-start rattle is the classic warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner, guides, and chain; inspect sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best for early intervention before engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain has snapped or caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV (2013-2018) currently values at £6,000-£14,000 depending on mileage, battery health, and specification. For vehicles under ~£8,000, a timing chain repair is almost always the better financial decision over a full replacement. For vehicles £8,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt 4B11 engine with warranty usually justifies the premium - especially if the vehicle has good battery health and you plan to keep it 2+ years. Replacement cost is typically 20-40% of vehicle value in the mid-range.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the timing chain rattle early, replace the chain and tensioner - it's far cheaper than a full engine. If the chain has already snapped or caused damage, a rebuilt or reconditioned engine with warranty is the sensible choice for any Outlander PHEV worth over £6,000. For very high-mileage examples with poor battery health, consider the scrap value first.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 4B11 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption (4B12) - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV 2.4L Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Piston ring wear can cause excessive oil consumption, particularly on vehicles with inconsistent servicing. Failed piston rings allow oil to enter the combustion chamber, causing blue smoke and potential catalyst damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip engine, replace rings, inspect bores
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early and bores are undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best if bores are scored or if vehicle is high-value

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV (2018-2022) values at £10,000-£22,000, making replacement a viable option. For vehicles under £10,000, evaluate the cost of repair versus the value carefully. For vehicles £10,000-£18,000, a reconditioned engine with warranty is generally the best long-term solution. Vehicles £18,000+ comfortably justify the premium of a rebuilt engine with upgraded components.
problems.recommendation: The 4B12 is a more robust engine than the 4B11, and oil consumption issues are less common than timing chain failures. If oil consumption is mild (under 1L per 1,000 miles), monitor it and keep oil topped up. If consumption is excessive, replacing piston rings is viable - but if the bores are scored, a full replacement engine is the right call.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 4B12 Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure (4N14) - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander DI-D 2.2 Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D (4N14, 2013-2018) - shared chassis with PHEV
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can leak coolant into the exhaust, causing white smoke, loss of coolant, and potential engine overheating. This is the most common 4N14 failure reported in the UK.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, flush cooling system, reset ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Best for early detection; typically resolves the issue without further damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if the engine has overheated from coolant loss and suffered head gasket damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: 4N14 Outlander diesel values typically sit at £5,000-£14,000. For vehicles under £7,000, an EGR cooler replacement is almost always the right decision. Full engine replacement only makes sense for vehicles worth over £8,000 with otherwise good condition and low mileage.
problems.recommendation: The EGR cooler failure is preventable with regular servicing. If you catch it early, replacement is straightforward and cost-effective. Full engine replacement is rarely justified for the 4N14 diesel unless the engine has been overheated to the point of head gasket failure or crankshaft damage.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV
finalCta.paragraph: The 4B11 and 4B12 engines are fundamentally robust units. With proper preventative maintenance and early intervention at the first signs of chain rattle or oil consumption, most Outlander PHEVs can run well past 150,000 miles. But if the worst happens, EnginesMarket connects you with UK specialists who supply reconditioned and rebuilt units with upgraded components addressing the original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty - and all at a fraction of main dealer prices.
